- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts show gradual upward drift, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 3–5% per period unless sentiment remains strongly bullish.
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model often underestimates downside — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model overfits recent volatility — smooth 30d forecast using 5-period moving average to reduce noise.
- When sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00), model often fails to adjust — force 3–5 period lagged mean reversion to true price.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong volatility, reduce forecast variance — use sentiment as volatility proxy (e.g., sentiment >0.5 → 10% std dev; <0.3 → 5% std dev).
